summary: Juliane Schober is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).

Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an academic post at Miami University.

Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and as a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting (1839–1913) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He later served as an honorary professor at Strasbourg and as Director of the National and University Library, Strasbourg.

Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen under doctoral supervisor Rudolf von Roth and earned a Lic. theol. at Jena (1880), later serving as Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Hoffory (1855–1897) was a linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen, Frederick William University Berlin, and the University of Strasbourg. He held an academic post at Frederick William University Berlin from around 1884 to 1889.

Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Leipzig, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He served as a professor at the University of Würzburg (1877–1920) and Tagore professor of law at Calcutta (1882–1883).

Julius Lipner (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Hywel David Lewis at King's College London. He taught at Birmingham and was Professor of Hinduism and Comparative Religion at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Pokorny (1887–1970) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna. He held posts at the universities of Vienna, Berlin (1920–1935), Bern (1944–1948), and Zurich (1948–1970).

Julius Schubring (1839–1914) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He pursued his university studies at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1857–1858), the University of Bonn (~1858–1859), and the University of Göttingen (~1859–1862).

Julius Zupitza (1844–1895) was a linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Moriz Haupt. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1869–1872), the University of Vienna (~1872–1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1876–1895).
Jun Fujii (born 1976) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who received his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2008 to 2013.

Jun Takashima (born 1955) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Minoru Hara at the University of Tokyo. He later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (Professor, 2020).

Jundo Nagashima is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Bristol under Paul Williams and also studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Taisho University and its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seung-suk Jung, Sungdoo Ahn, and doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson, earning a PhD from Hamburg in 2012. She also served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed a master's at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University (attested 2016) under the supervision of Stanley Abe.

Junjirō Takakusu (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president of the University of Tokyo, and led Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Toyo University and founded Sōgenkutsu in 1892. He held professorships at Toyo University and Komazawa University, and also taught at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (born 1935) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (professor and director), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
